protocol: The detector (`medbridge/privacy/redaction.py`) is rule based; it was developed only against the development set `tests/privacy/pii_testset.json` (v1.1, both its `dev` split and its earlier `heldout` split, which became development data once its misses were studied) plus self-authored probe sentences in `tests/privacy/test_redaction.py`.

The v1 held-out misses (names after 'its me X', 'my husband's name is X', 'Sign: X'; a +91 landline written with spaces; a PIN after a comma-separated locality) were fixed by general rules, not string-specific ones, and clinical values were re-checked.
The detector was then frozen; its SHA-256 is recorded below.

The blind held-out set `tests/privacy/pii_testset_blind_v2.json` was written by another author who did not read the detector, this script or its metrics. Only its header metadata (format, conventions, category counts) was read before the run, to make the loader accept its start/end offsets; no detector rule was added for anything mentioned only there.

The blind set was evaluated once with the frozen detector. The detector was not changed after seeing the results; problems found are listed as open issues instead. The report was regenerated afterwards with the same detector hash only to add the category-agnostic masking metrics and the post-hoc error analysis; every span metric is identical to the first run.
Development-set numbers are in-sample and optimistic; the blind numbers are the estimate of generalisation.

groups.description: NAME with no supported cue: the name opens the message, sits in a list or header, or is the object of a verb ('Anjali Bhosale, 47 - ...', 'Tanvir and Fatima', 'Claim form: X', 'ask X at the front desk'). Out of scope by design (cue-based names only, to protect drug and clinical words).

NAME after an English / Indian-English cue the detector does not know: 'X here', 'X this side', 'I X am', 'From: X', 'Me (X)', 'Sent by X', '- X' closing the message, 'name X' without a colon, 'Pt: X', and 'this is X,' with neither a greeting nor a 'calling/speaking' trailer.
NAME in SMS style: lower-case name after 'im' / 'this is', or a misspelt cue ('husbnd', 'doctr'). Capitalised-only cues miss them.
NAME after a Hinglish cue ('mera naam X hai', 'unka naam X', 'Beta X').
UK formats not supported (deliberately not added: they appear only in the blind set's metadata, not in the development data): NHS numbers, +44 phone numbers.
ADDRESS with a UK postcode: the locality extension stops inside the postcode ('Leicester LE' + '3 9QT'), leaving part of it visible (bug).

ADDRESS boundary errors on Indian / US formats: house numbers with a letter prefix or a slash ('B-12', '12/4', 'Quarter No. C-45', 'Gali No. 3'), the US abbreviation 'Dr' (Drive) and a directional prefix ('2205 W Belmont Ave'). Part of the address stays visible; in B2P130 the PIN too.
Other formats: scheme-less URL ('bpbuddy.app/...'), the DOB cue 'b.', and an ESIC 'IP number' redacted as MRN instead of INSURANCE_ID (the value is still masked; only the category is wrong).
False positive on a negative: the title cue 'Dr.' followed by a non-person word ('Dr. Google'). No clinical value was touched.
